Two defects in `provenance.mjs brief`, both found while backfilling the shelf. Advances #2169.

## Bug 1: a rule reworded in place was drafted as born at the rewrite

The brief finds a rule's history by walking back through its file's commits. At each older revision it looks for the same rule by slug, then exact trigger, then exact text, and it drafts `born` at the first revision where none of the three matches.

That works when a rule changes one thing at a time. It fails when a single commit changes all three inside the same file. The clearest case is #760, which rewrote `packs/basics/RULES.md` from prose paragraphs (each carrying four or five rules) into 61 situation-keyed bullets, "with every rule preserved". Before #760 the rule parser sees only 4 bullets in that file, so for 43 of the 61 rules the walk stopped at #760 and drafted it as their birth. #2248 fixed the case where a rule moves unchanged to another file or carrier. It didn't fix this one, because the rule never left its file: it just stopped matching. The four backfills corrected 151 false births by hand: 69, 13, 13, and 56 for `basics`.

**Fix.** When the exact match fails but the file still exists, the walk looks for the rule's own words (lowercased, four letters or more, common words dropped) in the older revision's passages, both bullets and prose paragraphs. If a passage holds at least 60% of them, that passage is taken as the rule before the rewrite:

- the rewrite commit is drafted `reworded`, not `born`;
- the walk keeps going back with the word set fixed at the rule's own text, because a paragraph carries several rules and its own words would drift onto its neighbours. It drafts `reworded` only where the rule's own words in that passage changed, and `born` where they stop appearing together;
- every rule followed this way is listed in a new section, **rules followed through an in-place rewording**, with its word share, so the backfill run checks it against `git show <sha>^:<file>`.

Two guards keep a split from being read as a rewrite:
- a passage another rule still matches exactly is that rule's older text, and can't be claimed;
- a passage that was one rule's own bullet goes only to the newer rule that holds most of it. When a rule is split off and the parent is reworded in the same commit, the split-off rule is born at the split. A prose paragraph can still feed several rules, which is the #760 shape.

**Measured** against the hand-corrected histories the backfills produced (each drafted born compared with the file's `born`):

| pack | right before | right after | newly right | newly different |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `basics` | 90 / 163 | 107 / 163 | 21 | 4 |
| local `claudinite` | 142 / 190 | 177 / 190 | 37 | 2 |
| `claudinite-growth` | 99 / 115 | 99 / 115 | 0 | 0 |
| `claudinite-canon-curation` | 31 / 49 | 31 / 49 | 0 | 0 |

For `basics`, false births at #760 fall from 41 to 6. Each of the 6 "newly different" is a replacement the backfill judged a new birth, where the draft now proposes continuity: `test-value-set`, whose #1734 title reads "widen the writing-tests rule", and `starting-change-will`, which #2016 reversed from an older rule. All six appear in the new section for the run to decide. The disagreements left in every pack are the cross-carrier and judgment cases the brief already reports in its other sections.

## Bug 2: a version row's text repeated once per commit it claimed

A `VERSIONS.md` row names every pull request it covers, so one row can claim many commits in the brief's commit inventory. The inventory printed the row's full text beside each commit it claimed. For `basics` the full brief came to 1,106,974 bytes, which I had to collapse by hand before one agent could read it.

**Fix.** Each inventory row now carries only `version <n>`. A new **version rows** section prints each claimed row once, with the commits it claims. The same brief is now 445,310 bytes, 40% of the old size.

## Other changes

- `backfilling-provenance/SKILL.md` names the two new sections, with a `reworded` entry on its provenance file.
- Tests: four new cases in `provenance-cli.test.mjs`: in-place follow with a contrast rule the rewrite really added, split off a survivor, split with the survivor reworded, and a row printed once.
